expectations.text: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
expectations.evidence: Intervals and confidence for every language

expectations.text: Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured
expectations.evidence: TOEFL and IELTS, learning intent explained

expectations.text: Response ranks or prioritises the five language audiences explicitly
expectations.evidence: VI 1st, TR 2nd, ES/DE lower, PL last

expectations.text: Ranking reasons use both audience size and growth (or intensity), not just one number
Response mentions that a language edition is not the same as a country (or gives a reader-geography caveat)
expectations.evidence: Names language editions as countries ('Іспанія', 'Німеччина', 'В'єтнам'), ignoring that es.wikipedia is mostly Latin America; also garbles the note ('Австрійські читачі блокуються')

expectations.text: Response notes that Wikipedia interest is not purchase intent or recommends validating with another signal
expectations.evidence: 'Википедія показує інтерес (цікавість), але не готовність платити'

expectations.text: Does not describe a change whose 95% interval crosses zero as growth (e.g. Turkish +7% [-20%, +43%] is 'no clear change')
expectations.evidence: '+7% (95% ДІ: -20% до +43%) – немає явного зростання, але й немає спаду'

expectations.text: Reasons are grounded in the data: no unsupported outside claims (competition, market size, demographics) or misreadings of the metrics presented as findings
expectations.evidence: Unsupported or garbled claims: VN audience 'практично 100% місцева', 'Австрійські читачі', wiki declines attributed only to 'технічні оновлення'
